title: Pre-Analysis (Closed) — Thrust Lever Friction Seal, Lubrication Interval Extension
abstract: Closed pre-analysis supporting the doubled lubrication interval on aircraft carrying the compatible friction seal, validated on twelve months of breakout force data from three operators.

sections.objective: Establish whether the lubrication interval could be doubled from twelve to twenty-four months on aircraft carrying the compatible friction seal and landed quadrant clamp, as assumed when the modification was released.
sections.findings_summary: Three items were confirmed and none blocking. Breakout force measurements from three operators over twelve months showed modified levers holding between seventeen and twenty newtons with no upward trend, against a delivered-seal population that rose measurably over the same period; that data is what supported the interval. The inspection task already reads the seal standard before comparing against the acceptance band, so it needed only an interval table entry rather than a rewrite. The autothrust troubleshooting entry sends the engineer to the breakout force check early, which becomes more important with a longer interval because the check is now the main opportunity to catch a drifting lever. One operator with mixed standards across its fleet asked for a single interval and was told no.
sections.next_steps: Interval extension approved for modified aircraft only. The mixed-fleet operator was given a per-aircraft interval table.

similarity_seeds: an interval doubled on the strength of one year of measurements

expected_findings.resolution: State in the task that the extended interval applies only when both levers are modified.
